subject: FinTechX POC: Observability & Success Criteria (Post-call recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Kim <jordan@fintechx.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechX POC: Observability & Success Criteria (Post-call recap)

Hi Jordan — thanks for the productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial observability plan. Please confirm and add any missing items.

Summary of what we covered
- Scope: 2-week POC to evaluate Redwood serving for customer-facing recommendation API (low-latency, token-cost sensitive).
- Goals: validate latency SLAs, measure cost per 1M tokens, ensure traceability for error/debugging, and verify integration with your monitoring stack.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms for typical 512-token requests under expected concurrency (see evaluation plan).
2) Reliability: <0.5% error rate for inference requests during steady-state load.
3) Cost: token consumption and unit cost measured and reported; target baseline to be compared to your current vendor.
4) Observability completeness: dashboards + traces capture request lifecycle, model version, and cache hit rate; logs exportable for audits.

Observability plan (high-level):
- Dashboards: latency (p50/p95/p99), throughput (rps), error rates, token usage per route, model version rollouts, KV cache hit rate.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans for request_received -> router -> model_inference -> kernel_exec; sample traces for 1% of traffic.
- Logs: structured JSON logs for each request, exported to S3 (30-day retention) and available via your SIEM.
- Metrics export: Prometheus endpoint + Grafana dashboard; alerts to slack (#fintechx-redwood-poc).

Technical/eval plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): finalize acceptance criteria, share access (SSO/SCIM or temp creds), provide sample traffic/requests.
- Week 1: onboarding + baseline runs, verify instrumented metrics and dashboards.
- Week 2: stress/soak tests, collect cost/latency report, final review and decision.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (engagement lead), Aditya (inference engineer), Marcus (solutions engineer).
- FinTechX: Jordan (product lead), Priya (SRE).

Requests from your side:
- Provide SSO/SCIM or temporary S3 access for log export and a sample set of representative requests (10-20k requests or a smaller anonymized sample).
- Confirm expected concurrency (qps) and any special routing by customer region.

Attachments: POC_observability_checklist.xlsx, mutual_action_plan.docx (MVP scope + timeline).

If that all looks good I’ll send a detailed observability checklist and schedule a 30-min kickoff for next week.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: FinTechX POC: Observability & Success Criteria (Post-call recap)

Great — thanks Jordan. Below is the more detailed observability checklist and ownership matrix we’ll use for the POC. I’m attaching a stub of Grafana dashboards (grafana-dashboards.json) for your SRE to preview.

Detailed observability checklist (to validate during Week 1):
- Dashboard: Latency Overview (p50/p95/p99) by route + breakdown by model variant.
- Dashboard: Throughput & Concurrency (rps, inflight requests).
- Dashboard: Error Rates & Types (4xx/5xx, model-timeouts, rate-limit drops).
- Dashboard: Token Consumption & Cost Estimation (tokens per request, tokens per route).
- Metric: KV Cache Hit Rate (percent).
- Tracing: Sampled spans for 1% of requests with attributes: request_id, route, model_version, prompt_length, response_length, kernel_exec_time.
- Logs: Request-level structured logs (JSON) with trace_id and request_id; export to S3 bucket or to your SIEM via Kinesis/Firehose.
- Alerts: p99 latency > 800ms for >5m OR error rate >1% for >5m -> notify #fintechx-redwood-poc and paged to Priya.

Evaluation plan and metrics to monitor during POC:
- Primary metrics: p95/p99 latency, error rate, KV cache hit rate, tokens per 1k requests, cost per 1M tokens.
- Secondary: model load (GPU utilization), kernel exec times, tail latencies per request length bucket.

Ownership and action items:
- Redwood (Aditya): instrument the Prometheus metrics, enable trace sampling, deploy Grafana dashboards, coordinate log export.
- Redwood (Marcus): run baseline traffic and help tune batching/quantization settings if needed.
- FinTechX (Priya): provide SSO/SCIM or temp S3/KMS access, and the sample request payloads.

Next steps (actions):
1) Jordan/Priya: share SSO admin contact + sample payloads by Mon 16 Mar.
2) Marissa/Aditya: prepare onboarding runbook + instantiate Grafana dashboard preview by Wed 18 Mar.
3) Schedule 30m kickoff the week of Mar 22 (Mar 23 preferred). I’ll send a calendar invite once we have confirmation.

Attachments in this email: grafana-dashboards.json (stub).

Thanks —
Marissa

Adding a few technical notes from the infra side to make the POC smooth.

What we need from FinTechX to onboard:
- SSO/SCIM admin or temporary AWS creds (S3 write + KMS decrypt) for log export. If you prefer, we can push logs to an S3 bucket in our account and give you read-only access.
- A sample of representative request payloads (10k recommended, 1k minimum) and expected qps (both steady-state and peak).
- If you have rate-limiting rules or custom middleware that mutates requests, share that code or behavior notes so we can reproduce.

Technical plan (short):
- We’ll spin a dedicated POC model variant pinned to the version we test; we’ll enable continuous batching with initial batch window set to 20ms and evaluate tradeoffs.
- We’ll instrument OpenTelemetry for spans and expose a Prometheus endpoint (metrics.retention=30d).
- Grafana dashboards will be imported from the attached stub and updated after baseline.

I’ll own the instrumentation and dashboard rollout. Marcus — will coordinate the baseline run with you and Jordan.

—Aditya
